question: After all three initial primes failed the surface-reduction gate, does the same direct detector give certified exclusions at a fixed larger prime panel?
selection: Keep exactly the same three translates and native triple. Use the first four primes at least131: 131,137,139,149. The first is already known to preserve the original surface and all twelve previous native branch divisors. Do not replace individual failed primes based on their outcomes.
method: Reuse the original direct equation-only detector and all its geometry, nodal-group, projective-chart and failure gates unchanged. No characteristic-zero intersection polynomial is an input. Compare with existing intersection certificates only in the later verifier.
failure_semantics: A bad surface/cover reduction remains UNKNOWN. A complete empty finite-field relation set proves a local obstruction only after every geometry gate passes. A nonempty set proves neither local lifting nor a global point.
boundary: A second fixed finite-field panel for the same retrospective relation constructions. It does not modify or enlarge the active curve search.
